title: Text may disappear with adjust_text
description:
I'm trying to recreate the fourth figure in [section 28.3 from R for Data Science](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/graphics-for-communication.html#annotations). The ggplot2 code is as follows:

```r
class_avg <- mpg %>%
  group_by(class) %>%
  summarise(
    displ = median(displ),
    hwy = median(hwy)
  )

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = class)) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(aes(label = class),
    data = class_avg,
    size = 6,
    label.size = 0,
    segment.color = NA
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

![](https://d33wubrfki0l68.cloudfront.net/7e8337dff68b63ffdc82a6e90d97aee522352803/6d5cb/communicate-plots_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png)

In plotnine, the text disappears when using `adjust_text`:

```python
from plotnine import *
from plotnine.data import mpg

class_avg = mpg\
.groupby("class")["displ","hwy"].median()\
.reset_index()

ggplot(mpg, aes("displ", "hwy", colour="class")) +\
geom_label(aes(label="class"), data=class_avg, size=16, label_size=0, adjust_text={'expand_points': (0, 0)}) +\
geom_point() +\
theme(legend_position="none")
```

![download](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1368256/67103546-a4f6cd80-f1c5-11e9-85fa-0c7e1fd30114.png)

When switching the order of `geom_point()` and `geom_label()` the text remains:

```python
ggplot(mpg, aes("displ", "hwy", colour="class")) +\
geom_point() +\
geom_label(aes(label="class"), data=class_avg, size=16, label_size=0, adjust_text={'expand_points': (0, 0)}) +\
theme(legend_position="none")
```

![download (1)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1368256/67103604-c061d880-f1c5-11e9-9acc-e40236d5de1d.png)

And interestingly enough, when adding another layer with `geom_point()`, the text remains and the points are on top, which resembles the original figure made in R.

```python
ggplot(mpg, aes("displ", "hwy", colour="class")) +\
geom_point() +\
geom_label(aes(label="class"), data=class_avg, size=16, label_size=0, adjust_text={'expand_points': (0, 0)}) +\
geom_point() +\
theme(legend_position="none")
```

![download (2)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1368256/67103645-d8395c80-f1c5-11e9-9a2b-b3722369dfcd.png)

So there's a work-around, but this might still be something worthwhile fixing. Hope this helps.

Thank you for this wonderful package.

Best,

Jeroen

plotnine gives unclear error and shows no violin plot, when a values appears to often in the to be plotted variable.

See the following example code:
```
import plotnine as p9
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

x = pd.DataFrame(data = np.array([np.ones(10), np.repeat(['A', 'B'], 5)]).T, columns=['ones', 'cat'])

p9.ggplot(x, p9.aes('factor(cat)', 'ones')) + p9.geom_violin()
```
Executing this example gives the following error:
`plotnine.exceptions.PlotnineError: 'Width not defined. Set with `position_dodge(width = ?)`'`

Running the same example in R ggplot2 produces a plot:
```
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)

 x = data.table(ones = rep(1, 10), cat = rep(c('A', 'B')))
ggplot(x, aes(cat, ones)) + geom_violin()
```

The same happens, when there is only a small fraction of other values in the data.

Thanks!

title: facet_wrap scales argument produces unexpected behaviour paired with coord_flip
description:
In many occasions I find myself using `geom_bar` to plot counts of categorical variables. To properly display the names of the categorical variable values' it is usually useful to make the bar's orientation horizontal. `geom_bar` will only compute the count groupying by the `x` aesthetic so the only way to force bars to be horizontal is to use `coord_flip`.  This works fine, for instance, with a minimal example:

```{python3}
from plotnine.data import msleep
(p9.ggplot(msleep)
+ p9.aes('order')
+ p9.geom_bar()
+ p9.coord_flip()
)
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10958332/60344648-4956c900-99b7-11e9-94dc-ee4ad04e4054.png)

However, if now we are interested in facetting by any other variable and we want to tweak the scales:
+ If we choose `free_x`, none of the axes becomes free:

```
(p9.ggplot(msleep)
+ p9.aes('order')
+ p9.geom_bar()
+ p9.coord_flip()
+ p9.facet_wrap('bodywt > 50', scales='free_x')
)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10958332/60344853-cb46f200-99b7-11e9-9629-174662120b97.png)

+ If we choose `free_y`, BOTH axes become free:
```
(p9.ggplot(msleep)
+ p9.aes('order')
+ p9.geom_bar()
+ p9.coord_flip()
+ p9.facet_wrap('bodywt > 50', scales='free_y')
)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10958332/60344874-def25880-99b7-11e9-89b5-89bf9ecd57d5.png)

Choosing `free` works as expected (and exactly equal to `free_y` in this case). 

Any idea or workaround on how to fix this?

title: Interactive pan & zoom with facets
description: Interactive panning and zooming in a Jupyter notebook (with the notebook backend) only affects the facet being manipulated. title: Cannot use logistic regression with stats_smooth
description:
Hey, really incredible work with plotnine!

I noticed recently that stat_smooth can take a custom method (e.g. glm), but since it doesn't pass `**method_args` when statsmodels initializes the glm, I'm not able to specify the family for the glm to use.

Here's the relevant [plotnine code](https://github.com/has2k1/plotnine/blob/97563c50d10deeb2d1c29d9e65e742c148db54ef/plotnine/stats/smoothers.py#L115).

Here's an [example](https://stackoverflow.com/a/17011659/1144523) of a logistic regression w/ stat_smooth in ggplot2

It looks like the `fit` method in the glm will ignore unused keywords, so I wonder if `method_args` could be passed both at model initializing and fitting? Maybe not the cleanest solution--I'm happy to look further into anything, if it's useful.

title: Scales, breaks and limits and transformations do not work as expected.
description:
```python
g = ggplot(diamonds)
g += geom_point(aes(x='carat', y='price', color='color'), stat='identity')
g += scale_y_continuous(name='price (USD)', 
    trans='log10',
     breaks=[100,1000,10000], labels=['100','1000','10000'])
g += scale_color_discrete(name='color (GIA scale)')
g
```
Expected: A plot.
Actual: Exception, 'Breaks and labels are different lengths. Make sure all the breaks you specify are with in the limits.'

Presumed reason: 100 is outside of the limits.

Ok, let's add some limits:

```g += scale_y_continuous(name='price (USD)', 
    trans='log10',
     breaks=[100,1000,10000], labels=['100','1000','10000'],
                       limits=[100, None])
```
Expected: Plot going from 100 to whatever the auto-training says the limit should be (see changelog for 0.3.0)
Actual: AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'log10'

```g += scale_y_continuous(name='price (USD)', 
    trans='log10',
     breaks=[100,1000,10000], labels=['100','1000','10000'],
                       limits=[100, diamonds.price.max()])
```
At last:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/51481268-c5f3d480-1d93-11e9-80b9-444dbf6abf50.png)

The first bug is independent of the transformation, it shows up as long as the break is outside of the limits.

The second one occurs only if the transformation is active.

First, thanks for developing this great package! As I understand the limitations of matplotlib do not make implementation of hatching easy (#238). I've created a workaround for my plots playing with matplotlib's figure obtained as shown in #63:

```python
p = ggplot() + ...
fig = p.draw()
axs = fig.get_axes()
for ax in axes:
    ax.spine['top'].set(...)
    xaxis = ax.get_xaxis()
```

While everything works perfectly, calling `p.draw()` causes the plot to be shown prematurely for me.
Would it be possible to prevent displaying the plot when calling the `draw()` method, for example with `draw(show=False)`? Or is there any other workaround?

title: stat_summary with geom='smooth' and colors

Using `stat_summary` for a group that is a continouse value works but yields a continous color scale:

from plotnine import *

 aes('variable', 'value', group='group', color='group') + 
 stat_summary(fun_y=np.median, geom='smooth'))

title: geom_crossbar as simple line
description:
In R/ggplot2 I can add a bar representing the mean via a gentle abuse of geom_crossbar:

```
library(RCurl)
library(ggplot2)

myfile <-getURL('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iaingallagher/BasicPython/master/data/marathon.csv')
mydat <- read.csv(textConnection(myfile), header=T)
head(mydat)
plt <- ggplot(mydat, aes(Gender, Time)) + geom_jitter(width=0.1) + 
stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", fun.ymin = "mean", fun.ymax= "mean", size= 0.3, geom = "crossbar", aes(width=0.35)) 
plt
```

In `plotnine` the geom_crossbar gives me a box in similar plots.

```
import pandas as pd
import plotnine as pn
pn.options.figure_size = (4,4)
import requests
import io

url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iaingallagher/BasicPython/master/data/marathon.csv'

data = requests.get(url).content
data_f = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data.decode('utf-8')))

jt_pt = pn.ggplot(data_f, pn.aes(x='Gender', y='Time')) + pn.geom_jitter(width=0.1) # jitter
jt_pt = jt_pt + pn.stat_summary(fun_data='mean_cl_boot', geom='crossbar', width=0.3, fill=None) # add mean
jt_pt
```

Is it possible to replace this box with just a line?

Thanks,

Iain

title: Legend order
description:
The legend order is not properly defined.
This code will produce both images on different invocations of the python interpreter:
```python
pdf = mtcars.assign(gear=pd.Categorical(mtcars.gear), am=pd.Categorical(mtcars.am))
pdf = pdf[sorted(pdf.columns)]  # should constrain, but doesn't.
p = (
    ggplot(pdf)
    + geom_point(
        aes("gear", "wt", shape="gear", color="am"),
    )
)
p

```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/48407180-888d1e00-e736-11e8-9adc-91a5a0975b60.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/48407295-c2f6bb00-e736-11e8-8173-6fd5b5b2f3ff.png)


My suggested fix would be to change line 308ff of guides/guides.py from
```python
for gdef in gdefs:
    if gdef.order == 0:
                gdef.order = 100         
```
to
```python
for ii, gdef in enumerate(sorted(gdefs, key=lambda gdef: gdef.title)):
    if gdef.order == 0:
                gdef.order = 100 + ii        
```

Which will still allow the user to set the order by hand if desired,
and would induce a simple alphabetical order otherwise.

We could also sort by DataFrame column order (followed by anything that's not a column, alphabetically), but it would be much more code, and I think not actually that transparent for the user.

ggplot2 doc states "if 0 (default), the order is determined by a secret algorithm.", so I guess sorting alphabetically would be ok then - at least it would be *stable*.

title: geom_rug needs to be changed when using coord_flip
description:
geom_rug takes a sides parameter (lrbt),
which is evaluated *after* the coord_flip.

This means you need to change your geom_rug call 
if you're adding a coord_flip() to a plot.

Example:
```python
import plotnine as p9
from plotnine.data import mtcars
g = p9.ggplot(mtcars,p9.aes('wt','mpg'))
g += p9.geom_point()
g += p9.geom_rug(sides='l')
g
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/47342065-02376c00-d6a3-11e8-97b3-7b0e7540eeb4.png)
and after the coord_flip:

```python
from plotnine.data import mtcars
g = p9.ggplot(mtcars,p9.aes('wt','mpg'))
g += p9.geom_point()
g += p9.geom_rug(sides='l')
g += p9.coord_flip()
g
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/47342084-15e2d280-d6a3-11e8-9d59-7d74cac5462e.png)


To my mind that is unfortunate, but required for full ggplot2 compability.

I have been thinking we might extend the accepted values of sides to include
perhaps y/Y/x/X which would read 'at y-axis, opposite y-axis ...', which would
flip 'correctly' when coord_flip is applied. 

This would maintain ggplot2 compability, while actually improving the situation.
The actual values are of course up to debate.
And it would cause an exception to use both kinds of sides at once in one geom_rug.

title: Discrete X axis is slow
description:
I have a use case where I need to sort my (discrete) x-axis by y-axis values.
I'd usually do this by turning it into a pd.Categorical,
and it works, but plotting is very slow.

Here's a minimal example with a 1000 points
which reports about 12 seconds on my machine:

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotnine as p9
pdf = pd.DataFrame({
    'x': [str(x) for x in range(0,1000)],
    'y': np.random.normal(0, 1, 1000)
})

g = p9.ggplot(pdf)
g += p9.geom_point(p9.aes('x','y'))
import time
s = time.time()
g.save("test.png")
e = time.time()
print('time for rendering', e - s, 'seconds')
```

The non-discrete scatter plot plotting
```python 
pdf = pd.DataFrame({
    'x': [x for x in range(0,1000)],
    'y': np.random.normal(0, 1, 1000)
})
```
takes 0.46 seconds!

Note that it's the cardinality of the x-axis, not the number of points as 
plotting ```'x': [str(x) for x in ['A','B'] * 500],``` is just as fast (or even faster) than plotting
continous data.

My debugging suggests that geom_point.draw_group is called once per x-value, leading to many many 
draw_unit and ax.scatter calls. 
This occurs because each data point get's it's own group.

Specifying a constant 'dummy group' by having a constant column 'group' in the dataframe and adding group='group' reduces run time by about half (12.3 vs 6.7 seconds). Better but not good.

How can we approach making this use case faster?

title: Non-aes x-value (and y?) treatment
description:
For *reasons* I wanted to create a jitter plot with a constant x-value,
which fails with an exception that "position_jitter requires the following missing aesthetics: x'" 
```g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y_column'), x = 1.0, position=p9.position_jitter(0.5, False)```

Thinking about this this has uncovered some inconsistencies in the way mappings are handled in kwargs,
which for color etc are *not* mapped:
```df = pd.DataFrame({
    'datax': ['shu','shu','shu'],
    'y': [1,2,3]})
g = p9.ggplot(df)
g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y', x='datax'), color='blue')
```
is valid while
```g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y', x='datax'), color='not-a-color')```
will throw an (expected) exception.

So far, so understandable.

But with x-values, weird things happen. 
```g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y', x='datax'), color='blue')``` => 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46741741-f2348b00-cca5-11e8-9dcc-9d1c30c0f8cc.png)

```g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y'), x = 'constant')```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46741767-fd87b680-cca5-11e8-8a99-76f2ab99ff11.png)

or with a numeric value
```g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y'), x = 5.0)```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46741799-0bd5d280-cca6-11e8-8dc4-205ee7444b01.png)

Note that 5.0 is simply outside the default limits, and  you can't add a scale with  appropriate limits to the last one, training will fail with an exception.
If you have points on the plot to train the axis though,
```
g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y', x='y'), color='blue')
g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y'), color='red', x=1.1)
```
this does get you an arguably correct plot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46742012-7e46b280-cca6-11e8-8fda-1f1ab7f21482.png)
with **mapped** values (try with x='y*100' and x= 150).

But this only applies to numerical values, even on discrete scales:
```
g = p9.ggplot(df)
g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y', x='datax'), color='blue')
g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y'), color='green', x='shu') # shows nothing
g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y'), color='red', x=1.1)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46742166-c6fe6b80-cca6-11e8-99c2-bb033b6ce642.png)


A long list of examples without much of a point, I guess - they just don't feel right.

I think at least ```g += p9.geom_point(aes(y='y'), color='green', x='shu')``` should throw an
exception. 

Being able to pass continuous numbers to a discrete scale - and have them
being interpreted as they are - is useful though, even if it's a bit inconsistent in that 
the euclidean scales always get their data mapped, while the others need literal values.

title: Points at 'infinity' can't be plotted
description:
One of the nicer hidden features of ggplot2 is that points with infinite value
are plotted 'half' at the border of a plot, like in this toy example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46215481-c3c9be00-c33d-11e8-99b5-05fb1062e44b.png)

Currently, potnine drops infinite values. 
Silently, unlike points otherwise outside the limit.
Even if the oob-function does return them, they're not plotted.

It would be nice to have this functionality in plotnine, at least optionally.
Together with an oob function that replaces values outside of the limits
with +-inf this would be really cool.

title: Default minor breaks on log scales are wonky
description:
The minor_breaks created by default on a scale_x/y_log10 are unintuitive.

Example:
```python
import pandas as pd
import plotnine
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0.1, 5]})
p = plotnine.ggplot(df, plotnine.aes('x','x'))
p += plotnine.geom_point()
p += plotnine.geom_point(data=pd.DataFrame({'x': 
    [ 0.082, 0.28, 0.46, 0.64, 0.82, 2.8, 4.6, 6.4, 5]
}), color='blue')
p += plotnine.geom_text(plotnine.aes(label='x'),
                    ha='left', nudge_x=.1)
p += plotnine.scale_y_log10()
p += plotnine.scale_x_log10()
p
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46151105-569b2780-c26e-11e8-8812-b311dcc67d41.png)

Note the blue dots, and their values that I reverse engineered out of a geom's panel_params.

Not that ggplot does it much better, placing a single minor tick sometwhere around Pi.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46151763-c6f67880-c26f-11e8-95ab-920af005404b.png)


Either way, the default minor ticks are worthless if the viewer can not
figure out what values they actually have.
My suggestion would be to either: Do not have default minor ticks on log axis,
or default to proper log ticks for base 10 and nothing for other bases.

title: Alpha appears to be ignored if it's constant for all datapoints:
description:
(why does github treat no text and enter as a valid issue... sorry about that).

An alpha aes is ignored when all instances have the same value.
Observe:
```python
p = plotnine.ggplot()
p += plotnine.geom_rect(
    plotnine.aes(xmin='xmin',xmax='xmax',ymin='ymin',ymax='ymax',fill='fill',
                alpha='alpha'),
          data = pd.DataFrame({
              'xmin': [0,0],
              'xmax': [1,0.5],
              'ymin': [0,0],
              'ymax': [1,0.5],
              'fill': ['red', 'blue'],
              'alpha': [0.5, 0.51]
          }),)
p += plotnine.scale_fill_identity()
p
```
Produces this, as expected.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46079830-85df6500-c198-11e8-8864-030adee6d1e4.png)

But replacing that second alpha value with 0.5:
```python
p = plotnine.ggplot()
p += plotnine.geom_rect(
    plotnine.aes(xmin='xmin',xmax='xmax',ymin='ymin',ymax='ymax',fill='fill',
                alpha='alpha'),
          data = pd.DataFrame({
              'xmin': [0,0],
              'xmax': [1,0.5],
              'ymin': [0,0],
              'ymax': [1,0.5],
              'fill': ['red', 'blue'],
              'alpha': [0.5, 0.50]
          }),)
p += plotnine.scale_fill_identity()
p
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1257580/46079858-9db6e900-c198-11e8-9666-6f1ee9333bcd.png)


I suspect this is also the underlying issue with #50  and #43 - arguably setting an aes to a scalar is something a user would expect - it's documented to work for x and y in the API.
But please note that this is a different case - we have a valid aes mapping that just happens to contain the same value for all instances and it's completely ignored :(.

title: Facet with geom_abline throwing errors and not working
description:
I am currently running into a couple errors when attempting to plot an `abline` for different facets. The first error involves not being able to set different slopes for different facets. The second error involves facet variables being reserved names.

Below is a reproducible example under version 0.4.0:
```
import plotnine as p9
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'list':['a','a','b','b'], 'x':[1,2,3,4], 'y':[1,2,6,8]})
df['category'] = df['list']
df_slope = pd.DataFrame({'category':['a','b'], 'intercept':[0,0], 'slope':[1,2]})
print(p9.__version__)
```
Plotting `points` with a facet works as expected:
```
(p9.ggplot(df, p9.aes(x='x', y='y')) + 
    p9.geom_point() +
    p9.facet_wrap('~category'))
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5490674/46040901-88ca4f00-c0df-11e8-8234-9ff58d2ad7fa.png)

Attempting to plot an `abline` with a facet throws an error.
```
(p9.ggplot(df_slope, p9.aes(intercept='intercept', slope='slope')) +
    p9.geom_abline() +
    p9.facet_wrap('~category'))
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5490674/46040890-823bd780-c0df-11e8-9fe2-cbac21841e59.png)

Attempting to plot both `points` and an `abline` does not throw an error, but it doesn't take the specified slope of `2` for facet `b`:
```
(p9.ggplot(df, p9.aes(x='x', y='y')) + 
    p9.geom_point() +
    p9.geom_abline(mapping=p9.aes(intercept='intercept', slope='slope'),
                   data=df_slope) +
    p9.facet_wrap('~category'))
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5490674/46040872-76e8ac00-c0df-11e8-8650-2afa91c67ae1.png)

Finally, there is another error that I'm getting when the name of the facet variable is reserved. When the variable is not reserved, everything works:
```
(p9.ggplot(df, p9.aes(x='x', y='y')) + 
    p9.geom_point() +
    p9.geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1) +
    p9.facet_wrap('~category'))
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5490674/46040858-69cbbd00-c0df-11e8-8195-30265ea47b13.png)

When the facet variable is reserved, I get another error:
```
(p9.ggplot(df, p9.aes(x='x', y='y')) + 
    p9.geom_point() +
    p9.geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1) +
    p9.facet_wrap('~list'))
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5490674/46040840-5d476480-c0df-11e8-961c-2ad110250081.png)

It seems like this issue has come up in the past, but it was thought to be fixed (#48).

title: Allow multi-index columns in aesthetics
description:
This doesn't have a parallel in R, but I think really affects usability in python with pandas.

While multilevel indices aren't tidy data, having multilevel column names doesn't break any tidy data rules, but we can't reference them.  Further more they get created a lot in pandas as a result of groupby aggregation, and they are not trivial to get rid of.  I don't know the internals, and since there is no R to copy, someone could choose the syntax that is easiest to implement; perhaps the most obvious would be to allow tuples in the aesthetic, since that is the equivalent accessor syntax in pandas.

Example:

```
df = pd.DataFrame(dict(A = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]*25, X = np.random.random(100), Y = np.random.random(100)))
print(df)
adf = df.groupby("A").agg(["mean", "median", "std"])
print(adf)

# Would be good to now be able to plot X:mean against Y:mean.  Something like
ggplot(adf, aes(x = ("X", "mean"), y = ("Y", "mean"))) + geom_point()

# The above doesn't work, instead you have to do something like this:

ggplot(adf, aes(x = adf[("X", "mean")], y = adf[("Y", "mean")])) + geom_point()```

I'm trying to save a series of plots as a pdf file using a generator and the save_as_pdf_pages() function in a jupyter notebook. The data is from a large file of drug treatmenrs, and I'm plotting the data for each drug separately. Thus, I've created a generator as follows:
`def plot_generator():`
`    for drug in drugs:`

I've simplified the actually plot code. When run independently, that works smoothly. My understanding is that I then should call save_as_pdf_pages() as follows:
`pn.save_as_pdf_pages(plot_generator(), filename='my_data.pdf')`
That call, however, yields the error:
`AttributeError: module 'plotnine' has no attribute 'save_as_pdf_pages'`
If I specifically import the ggplot class from plotnine, and call as:
`ggplot.save_as_pdf_pages(plot_generator(), filename='my_data.pdf')`
The error changes to:
`AttributeError: type object 'ggplot' has no attribute 'save_as_pdf_pages'`
When I leave the notebook and go to an iPython console, tab completion shows that the only methods in the ggplot class are draw, mro, and save. As the save_as_pdf_pages() is listed in the ggplot class on both the docs and the source code, this is odd! Has it's location moved?
I'm using plotnine v0.4.0 with python v3.6.6 installed with anaconda 5.2.

```
p = gg.ggplot(gg.aes(y='objective', x='value', fill='param'), df)
p = p + gg.geom_point(show_legend=False) 
p = p + gg.geom_density_2d(show_legend=False)
p = p + gg.facet_wrap('~ param', ncol=3, scales='free_x')

title: Confusing wording on aes grouping in the docs
description:
The docs on [`plotnine.aes()`](https://plotnine.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/plotnine.aes.html?highlight=group) run out of steam when they get to the "group" section:

>The group aesthetic
>
>group is a special aesthetic that the user can _map_ to. It is used to group the plotted items. If not specified, it is automatically computed and in most cases the computed groups are sufficient. However, there may be cases were it is handy to map to it.

How does one _map_ to something? I tried using map(), but didn't know what to use for the second argument. I tried a lambda, but that failed too:

    geom_boxplot(aes(group = lambda x: round(x)))

Error:

    plotnine.exceptions.PlotnineError: "Do not know how to deal with aesthetic 'group'"

Tracked down that error [in the code](https://github.com/has2k1/plotnine/blob/master/plotnine/layer.py#L338), but I still can't quite figure out how I'm supposed to use this. That method only seems to discuss types.

I'm hoping I can use it like `cut_interval()` and friends in ggplot2. I want all of my data on a given axis to be grouped into buckets like ((0,2], (2,4], (4,6], etc.).

Anyway, some more guidance in the docs would be really helpful here.

title: facet_wrap dir='v', ncol=N gives N rows instead of N cols
description:
A normal `facet_wrap` using the default `dir='h'`:
```py
(mpg
    .pipe(ggplot)
    + aes(x='displ', y='hwy')
    + facet_wrap('class', dir='h', ncol=4)
    + geom_point()
)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/627486/42836858-0a077630-89b1-11e8-9e3b-81742a48e193.png)

When you use `dir='v', ncol=4`, you get 4 rows instead of 4 cols:
```py
(mpg
    .pipe(ggplot)
    + aes(x='displ', y='hwy')
    + facet_wrap('class', dir='v', ncol=4)
    + geom_point()
)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/627486/42836861-124496b6-89b1-11e8-9001-2ea23e32dafb.png)

As a workaround, you can switch to `dir='v', nrow=4` to get 4 cols:
```py
(mpg
    .pipe(ggplot)
    + aes(x='displ', y='hwy')
    + facet_wrap('class', dir='v', nrow=4)
    + geom_point()
)
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/627486/42836863-159223c4-89b1-11e8-8248-73365a2a3cac.png)

If I draw a plot using IPython's implicit printing (not assigning the plot to any variable), as far as I know, there is no way to delete it, so the plot will keep appearing until I reset IPython.

title: Add helper to create a pdf document with a plot per page
description:
This is a request for an enhancement. I find myself writing a lot of code like this:
```python
from matplotlib.backends.backend_pdf import PdfPages
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import plotnine as p9

# (data loading code)

with PdfPages('output.pdf') as pdf:
    for label, group_data in data.groupby('foo'):
        plot = p9.ggplot(group_data) \
            + p9.geom_point()
            # (further geoms and plotnine stuff)
        fig = plot.draw()
        pdf.save(fig)
        plt.close(fig)  # save memory
```
and find myself wishing to do something like:
```python
plot = p9.ggplot(data) \
    + p9.facet_page('foo') \
    + p9.geom_point()
    # (further geoms and plotnine stuff)
plot.save('output.pdf')
```

At least three problems I can imagine:
- Only the PDF backend in matplotlib supports multiple-page files, and plotnine doesn't know until told to draw/save whether the user will be using PDF. If they are not, I guess, they would need to supply a callback like the `labels` argument to some scales that would generate the (base)name of multiple files; or the `filename` argument to `save()` would need to be a format string like `output-{foo}.png`; or something like that.
- “That's an abuse of the grammar of graphics; you should find a better way to plot your data.” This is true, but I find myself doing this while figuring out *how* I want to design more carefully-constructed plots.
- “This is too similar to `plotnine.Animation`,” though I think it's fairly distinct, just as the multi-page PDF and animation features of matplotlib seem to be distinct and target different use-cases.

A very brief skim suggests the existing faceting code seems more oriented at producing layouts on a single page, but with a few words of direction on how this should work I'd be happy to take a stab at it over the upcoming months.

title: Plotnine performance issue
description:
Firstly, thanks for creating this project - I've been looking for a python grammar of graphics implementation for a while.

I'm having a performance issue plotting a large Pandas data frame.

The data is found in `prob_w_d_df`, which is a `(600000, 3)` data frame; `prob_w_d_df.describe()` gives:

```
	doc_id		prob
	------		----
count	600000		6.000000e+05
mean	29		1.000000e-04
std	17.318117	4.862052e-04
min	0.000000	2.285988e-07
25%	14.750000	1.205222e-06
50%	29.500000	5.755733e-06
75%	44.250000	3.625872e-05
max	59.000000	9.012307e-02
```

The plot code is:

```python
ggplot(prob_w_d_df, aes(x='feature', y='prob', group=1)) + 
 geom_line() + 
 xlab("Word") + 
 ylab("P(word)") +
 facet_wrap('~doc_id', scales="free") +
 theme_minimal(base_family="Arial") +
 theme(figure_size=(15,15), axis_text_x=element_blank())
) 
```

This takes **1,543 seconds** (~27 minutes) to generate the plot.

Now I understand it's a large data frame so will be slow; however, when I replicate the exact above code with `ggplot2` in R it takes **65 seconds**. I understand R may be faster but the difference seems to great.

Is there anything I'm doing wrong or should do you improve performance?

(I've shared a CSV dump of `prob_w_d_df` if it helps: [`prob_w_d_df.csv`](https://drive.google.com/open?id=17rr13kH5uS2gwkf_-K9m60N0gWUwoy24).)

Thanks.

from plotnine import *

playSlider.observe(createPlot, 'value')

display(playSlider)

Using ```%matplotlib notebook``` or ```%matplotlib inline``` makes no difference, new plot are appended to the cell's output.

I did find the "_draw_using_figure" and "_create_figure" methods in the code, but my attempts to force new plots to be created in the same matplotlib figure were unsuccessful.

Is this a problem in the implementation or just me missing the correct syntax?

title: Unclear argument requirements in plotnine/stats/binning.py
description:
In `geom_histogram` the `breaks` argument is documented as _array-like_ which seems to mean "numpy array like in that it supports vector arithmetic and element wise multiplication". This means that simple specifications with python native data types, like `[x-.5 for x in range(10)]` are not supported unless one wraps the whole thing in an `np.array()`

Perhaps the function could cast the input sequence to the expected np.array data type or the line
`bin_x = (breaks[:-1] + breaks[1:]) * 0.5` could be made more general.

Assuming:

```
import itertools as itr
breaks = [x-.5 for x in range(10)]
```

Then:

```
a, b = itr.tee(breaks)
next(b)
bin_x = [(i+j)*.5 for i,j in zip(a,b)]
```

title: Problems using `scale_size_manual`
description:
I'm trying to use plotnine to build a plot with points sized based on their a classification 1-4.

In the MWE below, I've constructed a test dataset that matches mine.

    from plotnine import *
    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np

    a = pd.DataFrame(data={'a':4*list(range(4)), 'x':np.random.random(16), 'y':np.random.random(16)})

    ggplot(a, aes(x='x', y='y', size='a')) + geom_point() + scale_size_manual(values=(3,3,3,3))

However, when I run the code, I get the following message:

> TypeError: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale

Thinking that the problem was that the `a` column was non-categorical, I tried the following MWE:

    from plotnine import *
    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np

    a = pd.DataFrame(data={'a':4*list(range(4)), 'x':np.random.random(16), 'y':np.random.random(16)})

    a['a'] = a['a'].astype('category')

    ggplot(a, aes(x='x', y='y', size='a')) + geom_point() + scale_size_manual(values=(3,3,3,3))

However, this gives the error message:

> ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer

In R's ggplot, the following

    library(ggplot2)
    a = data.frame(a=rep(1:4,4), x=runif(16), y=runif(16))
    ggplot(a, aes(x=x, y=y, size=a)) + geom_point() + scale_size_manual(values=c(3,3,3,3))

gives the familiar message

> Error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale

Introducing a factor solves the issue:

    library(ggplot2)
    a   = data.frame(a=rep(1:4,4), x=runif(16), y=runif(16))
    a$a = factor(a$a)
    ggplot(a, aes(x=x, y=y, size=a)) + geom_point() + scale_size_manual(values=c(3,3,3,3))

title: plotnine: How to plot multiple variables on X-Axis?
description:
When plotting the diamonds.csv data, I recalled that the price of a diamond is really dependent on 4 variables, the carat size, clarity, cut and color. Using your previous suggestions on plydata.summarize, I created a modified X-Axis composite variable based on carat size & clarity.

I tried specifying a list of column names for the graph aes, but didnt get anywhere.

To create the composite variable, first I pandas.cut to map the various sizes into 4 bins, then pandas.assign to create a new column.
 `carat_sizes = pandas.cut(diamonds['carat'], [0, 1, 2, 3, 100], labels=["0-1", "1-2", "2-3", "3+"])`
`df2 = diamonds.assign(size = carat_sizes)`

Next step was to merge the clarity column with the newly added carat_size column. I didnt find any suitable functions to do this, so I coded the following:
`combo = []`
`for i in range(len(df2.values)):`
`   c = df2.loc[i,'clarity']`
`   s = df2.loc[i,'size']`
`   cs = c+" "+s`
`   # print("i:", i, "c:", c, "s:", s, "cs:", cs)`
`   combo.append(cs)`
`df3 = df2.assign(clarity_size = combo)`

Anyway, by plotting the 'clarity_size' combo index on the X-Axis, I was able to get the following graph:
![plotnine_plydata](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32575796/33730281-7d996512-db4d-11e7-88ca-bccfdf3966af.png)

Using the geom_text(angle=90), I was able to add labels rotated vertically. However the default text on the X-axis is still horizontal and cut off.

So my questions are:
1) Is there a more graceful way to plot multiple variables on the X-axis? Creating a composite single variable seems to go against the grain of the tidy data principles.
2) How to get the default text on the X-Axis rotated vertically? Playing with plotnine.scales.scale_x_continuous(angle=90) & plotnine.scales.scale_x_continuous(labels='') didn't work.

Here is the full script: 
[plotnine_plydata.zip](https://github.com/has2k1/plotnine/files/1540108/plotnine_plydata.zip)

```python
           {"timestamp": pd.Timestamp("2017-11-30 12:17"), "count": 2}, 
           {"timestamp": pd.Timestamp("2017-11-30 12:18"), "count": 3},

data = pd.DataFrame(entries)
ggplot(aes(x="timestamp", y="count"), data=data) + \ 
    geom_point() + \
    geom_vline(xintercept=data.timestamp[2]) + \
```

description:
First of all, thanks for the great implementation of ggplot2 for Python.

Unfortunately, I might have spotted an issue with the scaling of a smoothed facet plot. The following code creates a plot that starts at 0.01 based on the data:

    plot = (ggplot(df_docs_model) +
        aes(x='quarter_num', y='value', color='factor(topic)') +
        geom_smooth(method='loess', span = 0.1, alpha=0.2, size=2, show_legend=False) + 
        scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(1994, 2019, 2))) +
        scale_y_continuous(breaks=[y / 100 for y in range(0, 15, 1)]) +
        facet_wrap('~topic')) 

When I set the scale manually to make sure the y-axis starts by zero, the axis adjusts accordingly. As you can tell from the plots, however, the values between these figures differ. 
To set the y-scale I used the this statement:

        scale_y_continuous(expand = (0,0), limits = (0,0.1))

I suspect that the statement above restricts the data (only values between 0 and 0.1 are considered) instead of limiting the scale. Do I use the wrong statement? Or is this an issue in the present implementation? Thanks for any clarification.

title: How to set lower axis limit only
description:
To better appreciate relative differences, having plots starting at 0 is often required (e.g. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11214012/set-only-lower-bound-of-a-limit-for-ggplot)

In ggplot2 there are several options to achive this with options, e.g.
 the 'expand_limits' function,
`scale_y_continious(limits=c(0, NA))`
or `ylim(c(0, NA))`.

However I did not manage to replicate this function in plotnine, apart from calculating the limits 'manually' beforehand (see below). Is there any nicer way to do this?

```python
from plotnine import *
from plotnine.data import mtcars

ymax = mtcars['mpg'].max()*1.1
(ggplot(mtcars, aes('wt', 'mpg'))
 + geom_point()
+ ylim(0, ymax))`
```

Having a quick look at the code I can see that `cbook.boxplot_stats` is returning `-inf` for some things like IQR or min values which I guess is causing weirdness. 

```python
import pandas as pd
from plotnine import *

reprex = pd.DataFrame({'value': [0,0,1,5,100000,4739273,11,0.0001,0, 0.00001,0.00001,1,5,100000,4739273,11,0.0001,0.00001],
```

``` python
# Works
(ggplot(df, aes(x='variable', y='value', fill='category'))

)
```

title: when the default scale could be either discrete or continuous
description:
I have a request to support a frequent use case. (Apologies if I have just missed the way to do this, I looked!) There exist cases where a column could reasonably map to either a discrete or a continuous scale, and I would like a user option to specify which one to use. 

A common example is a data column that is integer type (defaults to continuous scale), but actually only takes on a handful of values in practice (meaning it could be reasonably mapped to a discrete scale). There is not an exact number of distinct values that can differentiate whether or not the integer variable should be treated as discrete or continuous, it ultimately depends on the user's need. From what I can see, plotnine assigns the default scale based on the pandas data type in the data frame, and thus the only way to change the default behavior is to mutate the data frame itself before creating the plot object. Obviously, mutating the dataframe works fine as a workaround.  

Here is my example: 
```
import pandas as pd
import random
import plotnine

df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [random.uniform(0,1) for i in range(15)], 
                   'b': [random.uniform(0,1) for i in range(15)], 
                   'c': [random.randint(0,5) for i in range(15)]
})

ggplot(df, aes('a', 'b', color='c')) + geom_text(aes(label='c')) + geom_line(aes(group='c'))
```

FYI: in R::ggplot2 I would accomplish this by casting the variable to a factor in the aes: 
```
ggplot(df, aes(a, b, color=factor(c)) + ...
```

In case it isn't clear, the reason this matters to me is it impacts how I can manipulate the color scale. For example, in the case where the integer code is binary, the default behavior is to assign the colors purple and yellow (extremes of the 'viridis' color scale), that yellow is an unfortunately hard to see default, and changing it is harder than it seems like it needs to be.

```
"statsmodels<=0.14.4; sys_platform == 'emscripten'"
```

This fixed it for Pyodide <314.0.0, where the vendored version of statsmodel was 0.14.4. However, nowadays, the vendored version is 0.14.6, so plotnine fails with the following error:

```
ValueError: Can't find a pure Python 3 wheel for: 'statsmodels<=0.14.4; sys_platform == "emscripten"'
```

Here are a few suggestions to fix this:
- Remove the `emscripten` line so that it works with modern versions of Pyodide (this will break it for older versions like Pyodide 0.29.4, but older plotnine versions could still be used)
- Use the following hack (Pyodide 314.0.0 bumped to Python 3.14) to make it work across Pyodide versions:
   ```
    "statsmodels<=0.14.4; sys_platform == 'emscripten' and python_version < '3.13'",
    "statsmodels>=0.14.6; sys_platform != 'emscripten' or python_version >= '3.13'",
   ```
- Make statsmodels an optional dependency

title: Feature Request: Plot compositions: collect axes (patchwork::plot_layout(axes="collect"))
description: Dear all, dear Hassan, First of all, thank you for this great package. I am trying to build some genomics plotting on plotnine. For example, I am trying to do upset plots using the new plot composition, like https://github.com/krassowski/complex-upset/ This is really a feature request, I realize how new the plot composition is. I need to align the axes of different plots in a composition, just like patchwork offers `axes="collect`, `axes="collect_x"`, or `axes="collect_y"` in `patchwork::plot_layout`. For getting the X-axis aligned here, I had to play around with margins a lot. Composing the composition further completely destroys the margins and axis alignment. Therefore, I wanted to ask if axis alignment in the plot-compositions would be possible or even on the plan already? Thank you and best regards, Max

title: Using `theme_matplotlib()` Raises `AttributeError`
description:
# Problem

Hi all, I'm using Plotnine for a first time. Currently migrating my visualizations from matplotlib and I've played around with plotnine's heatmap.

I found a possible bug when running `theme_matplotlib()`. The plot works fine without `theme_matplotlib()`, but has a problem when I add `theme_matplotlib()` to the `ggplot`

# Replicate
- Using dependencies
  ```
  matplotlib==3.11.0
  plotnine==0.15.8
  ```
- Run python via script mode (a `*.py` file, not `*.ipynb`)
  ```python
  from plotnine import (
      aes,
      geom_tile,
      ggplot,
      theme_matplotlib,
  )
  from plotnine.data import faithfuld
  
  plot = (
      ggplot(faithfuld, aes("waiting", "eruptions", fill="density"))
      + geom_tile()
      + theme_matplotlib()
  )
  plot.show()
  ```
- Expected outcome: a heatmap
- Instead I got error
  ```
  (.venv) PS C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts> & c:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Scripts\python.exe c:/Users/Grapes/Desktop/Workbench/plotnine-scripts/run_theme_matplotlib.py
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "c:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\run_theme_matplotlib.py", line 16, in <module>
      plot.show()
      ~~~~~~~~~^^
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\plotnine\ggplot.py", line 193, in show
      self.draw(show=True)
      ~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\plotnine\ggplot.py", line 304, in draw
      with plot_context(self, show=show):
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\plotnine\_utils\context.py", line 74, in __enter__
      self.rc_context.__enter__()
      ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
    File "C:\Program Files\Python313\Lib\contextlib.py", line 141, in __enter__
      return next(self.gen)
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\matplotlib\__init__.py", line 1210, in rc_context
      rcParams.update(rc)
      ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^
    File "<frozen _collections_abc>", line 987, in update
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\matplotlib\__init__.py", line 779, in __setitem__
      cval = valid_key(val)
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\matplotlib\rcsetup.py", line 310, in validate_backend
      if s is _auto_backend_sentinel or backend_registry.is_valid_backend(s):
                                        ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
    File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\matplotlib\backends\registry.py", line 224, in is_valid_backend
      if not backend.startswith("module://"):
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  AttributeError: 'object' object has no attribute 'startswith'  
  ```

# What I found
- I dug around the plotnine source code locally a bit and found `BackendRegistry.is_valid_backend` method with the if-check
  ```python
  if not backend.startswith("module://"):
      backend = backend.lower()
  ```
- Here, the argument `backend` is expected to be string, but instead it is received an `object`, not `str`. This raised the exception. I added a bandaid fix on my local installation to trigger its intended error message instead.
  ```python
  if not isinstance(backend, str):
      return False

  if not backend.startswith("module://"):
      backend = backend.lower()
  ```
- Running the heatmap python script, I get this message instead.
  ```
  File "C:\Users\Grapes\Desktop\Workbench\plotnine-scripts\.venv\Lib\site-packages\matplotlib\__init__.py", line 781, in __setitem__
      raise ValueError(f"Key {key}: {ve}") from None
  ValueError: Key backend: '<object object at 0x000001E0483EF970>' is not a valid value for backend; supported values are ['gtk3agg', 'gtk3cairo', 'gtk4agg', 'gtk4cairo', 'macosx', 'nbagg', 'notebook', 'qtagg', 'qtcairo', 'qt5agg', 'qt5cairo', 'tkagg', 'tkcairo', 'webagg', 'wx', 'wxagg', 'wxcairo', 'agg', 'cairo', 'pdf', 'pgf', 'ps', 'svg', 'template']
  ```
- I think this is the intended error message. After this message, I try changing my matplotlib backend to use something else, say `tkagg`:
  ```python
  import matplotlib
  from plotnine import (
      aes,
      geom_tile,
      ggplot,
      theme_matplotlib,
  )
  from plotnine.data import faithfuld
  
  matplotlib.use("tkagg")
  
  plot = (
      ggplot(faithfuld, aes("waiting", "eruptions", fill="density"))
      + geom_tile()
      + theme_matplotlib()
  )
  plot.show()
  ```
- This can now plot the heatmap as expected.
- I hypothesize the root cause being the method `BackendRegistry.is_valid_backend` receives an object instead of a string.
